exposure: slowing fetal growth velocity (EFW z-score change per week)
cohort: The study included 24,395 singleton pregnancies with at least two ultrasound fetal size assessments between 18+0 and 39+6 weeks.
finding: Slowing fetal growth velocity significantly increased the risk of perinatal mortality and adverse perinatal outcomes, with a growth rate slower than -0.13 EFW z-scores/week associated with a sixfold increased odds of perinatal death.
followup_time: Up to neonatal death (typically within 28 days post-birth) for perinatal mortality; up to birth for stillbirth.
